extracted.intended_audience: Parliamentarians, policymakers, agency administrators, and administrative law practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and recommended procedural rules for independent administrative agencies exercising statutory decision-making powers, aimed at guiding Parliament and agencies in structuring procedure, accountability, appointments, and powers. Focused on producing fair, effective, and accountable administrative decision making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and conflict_of_interest
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should be impartial in carrying out its duties as a statutory decision maker. Members should be required, while holding office, to divest their conflicting financial interests, to disclose those of their spouses and close relatives, and to withdraw from individual proceedings whenever, for any reason, there is a reasonable apprehension of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to members while holding office; includes divestment, disclosure, and withdrawal from proceedings on reasonable apprehension of bias. Confidentiality accommodations may apply where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoned_decisions_for_adverse_outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should give reasons for a decision whenever the decision amounts to a total or partial denial of a requested action, or is otherwise adverse to the interests of a participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision of reasons is required for denials or other adverse actions to ensure transparency and accountability to participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration_and_review
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should provide for the reconsideration or review of its decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must adopt internal mechanisms allowing review or reconsideration of decisions to address errors or change in circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliamentary_empowerment_to_secure_information
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to secure information that is relevant to the matter in question, including the power to summon witnesses and documents during any proceeding at which a decision must be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should have statutory powers to obtain evidence necessary for decision making, akin to summons powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control_over_proceedings_and_removal_of_disruptors
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to maintain control over its proceedings and to remove disruptive persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies need authority to manage their hearings and ensure orderly proceedings, including removing disruptive attendees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power_to_initiate_contempt_proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to initiate contempt proceedings in the Federal Court of Canada.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides agencies remedies to enforce compliance with their processes through the Federal Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power_to_compel_preliminary_sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to compel preliminary sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority to require pre-hearing or preliminary conferences to prepare matters for substantive decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power_to_adjourn_proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to adjourn proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexibility to delay hearings where warranted, as part of procedural authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power_to_make_interim_orders_and_relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to make interim orders and to provide interim relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows agencies to grant temporary measures pending final decision to protect parties or the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power_to_adjust_proceeding_format
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to adjust from an adjudicative to a rule-making format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should be able to change the mode of action (e.g., from individual adjudication to rule-making) when appropriate to address issues effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power_to_add_participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to add participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may admit additional parties or intervene where necessary for a just resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power_to_consolidate_proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament should empower agencies with the power to consolidate proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation authority helps avoid duplication, inconsistent decisions, and inefficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency_developed_rules_of_evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where otherwise specifically prescribed by statute, an agency should not be obliged to follow the rules of evidence that apply in courts of law, other than the rules of evidentiary privilege. Rules of evidence should be developed by agencies as incidents of administrative procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should craft evidence rules suited to administrative context while preserving privilege protections; courts' technical evidence rules need not bind agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency_rulemaking_and_periodic_review_of_procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should be encouraged to make and review periodically rules of procedure, using the legislated standards as guidelines. By the same account, Parliament should refrain, wherever possible, from inserting detailed procedural requirements in agency legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should own their procedural rules, review them periodically, and ground them in legislated standards; Parliament should avoid over-prescriptive procedural statute language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliamentary_scrutiny_but_no_judicial_review_for_nonconformity
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules of procedure an agency adopts should be subject to scrutiny by a parliamentary committee, and to disallowance in Parliament, but not to judicial review on grounds of non-conformity with the standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parliamentary oversight (committee review and disallowance) is the check on agency procedural rules; courts should not review agency procedural rules simply for departure from legislated procedural standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory_body_reporting_on_procedural_rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An advisory body comprising representatives of public and private sector institutions having an interest in the federal administrative process should be required to file with the parliamentary committee that considers a set of agency rules of procedure a report of its assessment of the appropriateness of these rules. This report should be filed through a politically responsible official such as the Attorney General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalizes stakeholder input into parliamentary review via an advisory body's report submitted through the Attorney General.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model_rules_of_procedure_development
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should be undertaken to develop a series of model rules of procedure that would accommodate different decision-making styles and activities. These models should serve as the starting-point for the development of rules of procedure by any newly created agency, and for periodic review by an existing one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model rules to reduce unnecessary diversity and serve as templates for new agencies and reviews of existing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political_onus_to_justify_deviations_from_models
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should have the political onus, when adopting rules of procedure, to justify deviations from the model rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agency departs from model rules it should publicly justify the deviation, placing the burden on the agency to explain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated_procedural_framework_and_information_sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Further work should be undertaken towards improving the information sharing, education, consultation, screening and co-ordination that are required for an integrated procedural framework for agency decision making at the federal level. In this respect, further consideration should be given to the creation of a permanent administrative council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for system-level coordination mechanisms (information sharing, education, consultation, screening) and possible permanent council to integrate procedures across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance_of_values_in_decision_making
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency decision making should achieve an appropriate blend of values such as fairness and accountability with those of effectiveness, economy and efficiency; values such as authoritativeness and integrity are particularly important where Parliament places decision-making responsibilities in a body outside the departmental structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural and structural design should explicitly balance these values; the Charter's values should be given place by Parliament and agencies as well as courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct_accountability_to_parliament_as_buffer
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct agency accountability to Parliament is recommended to reinforce the independence of the agency by providing a buffer between it and the executive. Parliament must become more active in evaluating execution of legislative objectives and allocate resources to perform this role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifts some oversight from executive to parliamentary processes to safeguard independence while ensuring accountability; requires parliamentary resource allocation and possible role realignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open_and_consultative_appointment_processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The appointment process should be reformed: each minister responsible for recommending a filling of an appointed position should invite applications and nominations; consult the head of the agency; consult the private sector and provincial governments where relevant; constitute an advisory committee to assist selection; and use testing and interviewing skills to produce a short list of the best qualified candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replaces 'anointments' with transparent, consultative selection practices to enhance credibility and political commitment to agency roles; room for experimentation in selection mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment_security_and_career_development
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns about short terms and vulnerability of appointees suggest considering a stronger career line within the federal administrative system, more tenure or stability, greater personal rewards, and easier re-entry to former careers to attract highly competent administrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider trade-offs of increased tenure and career structures; objective is to attract and retain qualified, dedicated administrators and reduce deterrents like stringent divestment requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate_appeal_arrangements_and_rationalization
rubrics_metrics.description: To properly handle 'dissatisfied customers', adequate appeal arrangements are required. Consideration must be given to rationalizing the existing patchwork of external appeals to agencies independent of the original decision makers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study and reform of administrative appeals is underway; aim to simplify and make appeals coherent across the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage_efficiency_without_sacrificing_fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are likely to face expanding workloads with fewer resources; specific limited measures should be considered to achieve greater efficiency in agency administration without undue sacrifice of the fairness essential to maintaining integrity of agency decision making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many practicable measures exist that agencies can implement directly without legislative reform; consult broadly to ensure practicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption_for_departmental_administration
rubrics_metrics.description: The presumption in structuring government machinery should be that administrative authorities be established within departmental confines unless there are very good reasons for constituting them as independent agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent agency model should not be automatic; agencies must be justified when chosen and incremental improvements pursued when model is selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency_and_consolidation_of_jurisdictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Work towards greater consistency in federal administrative procedure, development of procedural models, more effective coordination and screening, and streamlining by consolidating jurisdictions where appropriate; some jurisdiction may be transferred from independent agencies into government departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to avoid proliferation of anomalous and unnecessarily individualized approaches, reducing costs and improving efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect_and_use_statistical_information_on_agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a need for comprehensive statistical information about agency organization and process to help ensure that organizational patterns are adequately attuned to processes for policy and decision making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support ongoing data collection programs (e.g., extend pilot projects) to inform reforms and internal adjustments.
